_note: Every elemental reaction, read by genshin-reactions.js (the Lobby wheel + /genshin-impact/reactions). Facts: Genshin Impact Wiki (Fandom, CC BY-SA) + the in-game tutorials, checked Oct 26 2026 for 7.1; research notes in docs/genshin-reactions-research.md. pair = the two elements that trigger it on the wheel (with = the partners for Swirl / Crystallize); on = a follow-up that needs another reaction first; swap = the reaction it replaces when one of `by` is in the party; coef = Base Reaction Coefficient x the level multiplier; dmg = which EM formula (trans 16, lunar 6, add 5, amp 2.78).

families.name: Amplifying
families.line: Make one hit bigger: the hit that sets them off is multiplied, and it can crit.

families.name: Transformative
families.line: Deal a separate hit of their own, from your level and Elemental Mastery. They can't crit, and enemy DEF doesn't matter.

families.name: Catalyze
families.line: Quicken gets the enemy ready; after it, Electro and Dendro hits get bonus damage (Aggravate and Spread).

families.name: Control & shields
families.line: Deal no damage: they freeze enemies or drop a shield to pick up.

families.name: Lunar
families.line: From Nod-Krai: three Hydro reactions that change into stronger versions when the right character is in your team.

families.name: Stellar Glimmer
families.line: From Snezhnaya: two Cryo reactions that change into stronger versions when the right character is in your team.

reactions.name: Vaporize
reactions.desc: Hydro meets Pyro and the hit that caused it gets bigger: 2× when you hit a Pyro enemy with Hydro, 1.5× when you hit a Hydro enemy with Pyro.
reactions.tip: The 1.5× way uses up less of the element already on the enemy, so you can trigger it again sooner.

reactions.name: Melt
reactions.desc: Pyro meets Cryo and the hit that caused it gets bigger: 2× when you hit a Cryo enemy with Pyro, 1.5× when you hit a Pyro enemy with Cryo.
reactions.tip: Frozen enemies melt too: hit a Frozen enemy with Pyro to trigger Melt.

reactions.name: Overloaded
reactions.desc: A Pyro explosion that hits every enemy around the target and knocks them away.
reactions.tip: Great on groups of weak enemies, annoying when it blasts them out of reach.

reactions.name: Superconduct
reactions.desc: Cryo damage in an area that makes enemies take more Physical damage: their Physical RES drops 40% for 12 seconds.
reactions.tip: Made for Physical teams: the resistance drop is the point, not the damage.

reactions.name: Electro-Charged
reactions.desc: Both elements stay on the enemy, and it takes Electro damage every second until one runs out. Each hit also jumps to one nearby wet enemy.
reactions.tip: Because both elements stay on, a third element can set off two reactions at once.

reactions.name: Frozen
reactions.desc: Locks the enemy in ice. Keep hitting it with Hydro and Cryo to keep it frozen; a heavy hit breaks the ice (Shatter).
reactions.tip: Bosses can't be frozen, so Freeze teams shine against groups of smaller enemies.

reactions.name: Swirl
reactions.desc: Anemo picks up Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo from the enemy and spreads it to every enemy around, dealing that element's damage.
reactions.tip: The spread element can react again: swirl Pyro onto wet enemies and they Vaporize.

reactions.name: Crystallize
reactions.desc: Geo knocks a crystal of the other element off the enemy. Pick it up for a shield that's strongest against that element.
reactions.tip: You have to pick the crystal up: walk over it before it fades.

reactions.name: Bloom
reactions.desc: Makes a Dendro Core that explodes after a few seconds, hitting enemies around it with Dendro damage. It can hit you too.
reactions.tip: Only 5 cores fit at once: a sixth makes the oldest explode right away.

reactions.name: Burning
reactions.desc: Sets the enemy on fire: Pyro damage over time to it and anyone standing in the flames, and it keeps putting Pyro back on them.
reactions.tip: It hits four times a second, which keeps Pyro on the enemy for Vaporize or Melt.

reactions.name: Quicken
reactions.desc: Marks the enemy as Quickened. Nothing happens yet: the next Electro hit gets Aggravate, the next Dendro hit gets Spread.
reactions.tip: Quicken deals no damage itself. The reward is every hit after it.

reactions.name: Aggravate
reactions.desc: An Electro hit on a Quickened enemy gets bonus damage added on top. The bonus grows with your level and Elemental Mastery.
reactions.tip: The bonus is added before the crit roll, so when the hit crits, the bonus crits too.

reactions.name: Spread
reactions.desc: A Dendro hit on a Quickened enemy gets bonus damage added on top. The bonus grows with your level and Elemental Mastery.
reactions.tip: A little stronger than Aggravate: 1.25× against 1.15×.

reactions.name: Hyperbloom
reactions.desc: Hit a Dendro Core with Electro and it turns into a shot that chases one enemy.
reactions.tip: The shots chase enemies, never you: the safe way to play Bloom.

reactions.name: Burgeon
reactions.desc: Hit a Dendro Core with Pyro and it explodes in a bigger blast.
reactions.tip: The blast can hurt your own character, like Bloom.

reactions.name: Shatter
reactions.desc: A heavy hit (a claymore, a plunging attack or Geo) breaks a Frozen enemy's ice for Physical damage.
reactions.tip: Breaking the ice ends the freeze, so Freeze teams usually avoid it.

reactions.name: Lunar-Charged
reactions.desc: A thundercloud appears and, every 2 seconds, strikes every nearby enemy with both Electro and Hydro on it. The strike adds up the hits of everyone who put those elements on, and it can crit.
reactions.tip: Only one cloud at a time. Trigger it again and the cloud's 6-second timer starts over.

reactions.name: Lunar-Bloom
reactions.desc: Dendro Cores still appear like normal Bloom, and your team also collects Verdant Dew. The reaction itself deals no damage: some characters' attacks deal Lunar-Bloom damage, often by spending the Dew.
reactions.tip: Verdant Dew never runs out: it stays through team swaps, teleports, the daily reset and even closing the game.

reactions.name: Lunar-Crystallize
reactions.desc: Three Moondrifts appear around the enemy. Every third time you trigger it, they fire Moondrift Harmony: a shot that chases enemies for Geo damage, adding up the hits of everyone who put an element on. It can crit.
reactions.tip: Moondrifts count as Geo constructs: with two Geo characters, Geo Resonance's +15% DMG turns on even without a shield.

reactions.name: Stellar-Conduct
reactions.desc: A Starlight Prism turns the area into a Polestar Field for 7 seconds: more Cryo and Electro damage, and enemies' Physical RES drops 40%. Every 4 seconds the field counts your Cryo and Electro hits and gets stronger. The reaction itself deals no damage: it comes from characters' attacks.
reactions.tip: In Snezhnaya's open world the field also keeps you warm and powers up Prime Ice constructs and firearms.

reactions.name: Stellar Swirl
reactions.desc: A hit of Anemo damage, then a Stellar Vortex that explodes into Cryo around it. Trigger it three times and the Vortex grows (Lv. 2) and hits harder; three more and it explodes at once.
reactions.tip: When a Vortex explodes, your next jump within 5 seconds goes higher.
